To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
auditors' work style, their perceptions of internal auditors' objectivity and competence, and the interaction of these variables, influence external auditors' judgments of internal auditors.

(a) auditors' working styles significantly influence the extent of planned testing and reliance judgments, (b) auditors' perceptions of internal auditors' objectivity and competence significantly influence the extent to which they rely on the work done by internal auditors, and (c) auditors' work style and perceptions of internal auditor competence and objectivity interact in influencing the extent to which auditors rely on internal auditors.

external auditors' judgments about the extent of reliance on internal auditors' work are affected by their work style, their previous perceptions about internal audit competence and objectivity (which may be influenced by their work styles), and their previous experience with barriers to internal/external auditor cooperation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which external and internal auditors can cooperate in the planning, conduct, and reporting of financial statement audits.
the extent to which external and internal auditors rely on each other and the factors that influence these judgments.
the factors that influence auditors' reliance decisions and the resulting audit testing and analytical procedures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

external auditors' reliance on the work of other professionals (i.e., internal auditors) is influenced by their own work style, their perception of the internal auditor's competence, and their perception of the competence and objectivity of the internal auditor.

the work style of external auditors and their perceptions of internal auditors' objectivity and competence significantly influence the extent to which external audit firms plan to rely on the results of internal auditors.

the external auditor's reliance on the work of the internal auditor is affected by both the external auditor's work style and the external auditor's perception of the internal auditor's competence and objectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
external auditors' reliance on the work of their internal counterparts is influenced by both external (environmentally based) and internal (affectively and cognitively based) factors.

external auditors' reliance on the work of their internal counterparts may be influenced by the auditors' work style, as well as the auditors' perceptions of the competence and objectivity of their internal audit partners.
auditors' work style and previous experiences influence the extent to which external and internal auditors rely on each other's work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
auditors' work style and their perceptions about internal auditions' competence and objectiveness influence their judgments about internal auditor reliance.

auditors' work style and perceptions of the internal auditor's competence and objectivity significantly influence the extent of planned reliance on the internal auditor and the interpretation of analytical procedures.
external auditors' reliance on internal audit is not a simple decision task.
